translationRepairs: [Tang Records 9] From the ninth month of the fourth year of Zhenguan through the seventh year of Zhenguan—a span of somewhat more than three years.

[Tang Records 9] From the ninth month of the zhuyong-kundun (wuzi) year, the second year of Zhenguan, through the chongguang-shanyan (xinmao) year, the fifth year of Zhenguan—a span of somewhat more than three years.
The cyclical years 著雍困敦 (wuzi) and 重光單閼 (xinmao) are Zhenguan 2 and Zhenguan 5; the current idiomatic text wrongly says Zhenguan 4 through Zhenguan 7.

In the second month, on wuyin, Fang Xuanling was appointed Left Vice Director and Du Ruhui Right Vice Director; Wei Zheng, Right Assistant Director of the Secretariat, was named acting Secretariat Director and admitted to deliberations on state affairs.

In the second month, on wuyin, Fang Xuanling was appointed Left Vice Director and Du Ruhui Right Vice Director; Wei Zheng, Right Assistant Director of the Department of State Affairs, was named acting Director of the Palace Library and admitted to deliberations on state affairs.
尚書右丞 is the Right Assistant Director of the Department of State Affairs (尚書省), and 秘書監 is the Director of the Palace Library, not a Secretariat (中書) post; the current text mistranslates both offices.
He therefore ordered: "Detailed Secretariat business should fall to the left and right assistants, and only major matters requiring memorial should be brought to the Vice Directors."

He therefore ordered: "Routine business of the Department of State Affairs should fall to the left and right assistant directors, and only major matters requiring memorial should be brought to the Vice Directors."
尚書 here is the Department of State Affairs whose Vice Directors (僕射) are addressed, not the Secretariat (中書); 細務 is routine business.

On bingzi the Xueyantuo khan Piluo sent his younger brother Tongte'er to pay tribute. The emperor gave him a precious sword and whip and said, "Among your followers, execute those guilty of great crimes and whip those guilty of lesser ones."

On bingzi the Xueyantuo Pijia Khagan sent his younger brother Tongte'er to pay tribute. The emperor gave him a precious sword and whip and said, "Among your followers, execute those guilty of great crimes and whip those guilty of lesser ones."
毘伽可汗 is the title Pijia (Bilge) Khagan of the Xueyantuo ruler Yinan (cf. 真珠毘伽可汗 and s0142a 夷男); the current text corrupts it into a personal name "Piluo".
On gengyin the Turk Yugushe led his following to surrender.
On gengyin the Turkic Yusheshe led his following to surrender.
郁射設 is Yusheshe (Yushe Shad); the current text renders it "Yugushe", confusing him with 欲谷設 (Yugushe) named earlier.

Fang Xuanling and Wang Gui conducted the evaluation of inner and outer officials; Investigating Censor Quan Wanji of Wannian memorialized that it was unfair, and the emperor ordered Hou Junji to investigate.

Fang Xuanling and Wang Gui conducted the evaluation of inner and outer officials; Quan Wanji of Wannian, Attendant Censor for Documents, memorialized that it was unfair, and the emperor ordered Hou Junji to investigate.
治書侍御史 is the Attendant Censor for Documents (zhishu shiyushi), not an Investigating Censor (監察御史).
he sent Zhisi-li to court to confess his offenses, offer the submission of the whole nation, and pledge to come in person to pay homage.
he sent Zhishi Sili to court to confess his offenses, offer the submission of the whole nation, and pledge to come in person to pay homage.
執失思力 is Zhishi Sili (clan Zhishi, name Sili); "Zhisi-li" garbles the name.
When Jiali's rule fell into disorder, Sunishi alone among those who had lost their divisions did not waver in loyalty.
When Jiali's rule fell into disorder, Sunishi's following alone did not waver in loyalty.
蘇尼失所部獨不攜貳 says only that Sunishi's tribes alone stayed loyal; "among those who had lost their divisions" is not in the source.
When Tuli had fled to Tang, Jiali had established him as Lesser Qaghan.
When Tuli fled to Tang, Jiali made Sunishi Lesser Qaghan.
In 頡利立之為小可汗 the object 之 is Sunishi, the subject of this passage, not Tuli; the current "him" misleads the reader into thinking Tuli was made Lesser Qaghan.
When Jiali was defeated and fled, he went to rely on him, intending to flee to Tuyuhun.
When Jiali was defeated and fled, he went to take refuge with Sunishi, intending to flee on to Tuyuhun.
Clarifies the referents of 往依之: Jiali went to rely on Sunishi; the current "he went to rely on him" is ambiguous.

The emperor admonished him, "Your ancestor Qimin threw himself into Sui's arms; Sui installed him as Great Qaghan and he briefly held the northern wilderness. Your father Shibi in turn became Sui's scourge.

The emperor admonished him, "Your grandfather Qimin threw himself into Sui's arms; Sui installed him as Great Qaghan and he came to possess the whole northern wilderness. Your father Shibi in turn became Sui's scourge.
奄有北荒 means "came to possess all the northern wilds", not "briefly held"; 祖 here is Tuli's grandfather Qimin (father of Shibi).
After a while, the emperor said, "Under the Sui, Shi Wansui defeated Qaghan Toutou—his merit went unrewarded, and he was executed for a crime.
After a while, the emperor said, "Under the Sui, Shi Wansui defeated Datou Qaghan—his merit went unrewarded, and he was executed for a crime.
達頭可汗 is Datou (Tardu) Qaghan of the Western Turks; "Toutou" misreads 達.

Shaboluo, khan of the Western Turks, was the late khan's son and won broad allegiance. Many of Moheduo Khan's chieftains went over to him. Shaboluo marched against Moheduo, routed his forces, and pursued him to Mount Jin, where the Nishoushe commander killed him; the tribes then jointly raised Shaboluo to great khan.

Si Yehu Khan of the Western Turks, being the late khan's son, won broad allegiance, and many of Moheduo Khan's chieftains went over to him. Si Yehu marched against Moheduo and routed his forces; Moheduo fled to Mount Jin, where he was killed by Nishou Shad, and the tribes then jointly raised Si Yehu as great khan.
肆葉護 is Si Yehu (not "Shaboluo"); 泥熟設 is Nishou Shad, a person, not a "commander"; Moheduo fled on his own, he was not pursued.
On jiaxu he banqueted King Wen Tai of Gaochang along with his ministers.
On jiaxu he banqueted Qu Wentai, King of Gaochang, together with the assembled ministers.
文泰 is the given name of Qu Wentai; "King Wen Tai" splits it wrongly.
On bingzi he returned to the palace and personally presented his quarry to the retired emperor at Dayan Palace.
On bingzi he returned to the palace and personally presented his quarry at the Da'an Palace, residence of the Retired Emperor.
大安宮 is the Da'an Palace, not "Dayan".
In the sixth month, on jiayin, Li Gang, Junior Tutor to the Heir Apparent and Duke Zhen of Xinchang, died.
In the sixth month, on jiayin, Li Gang, Junior Preceptor of the Heir Apparent and Duke Zhen of Xinchang, died.
太子少師 is Junior Preceptor (少保 was Junior Guardian/Tutor), matching s0352.
Earlier, the widow of Yuwen Xian, Prince of Qi of Northern Zhou, who had no children, had been supported with great generosity by Li Gang.
Earlier, the daughter of Yuwen Xian, Prince of Qi of Northern Zhou, widowed and childless, had been supported with great generosity by Li Gang.
憲女 is Yuwen Xian's daughter (who was a widow), not his widow.

Imperial Censor Quan Wanji impeached Zhang Yungu: "Yungu is registered in Xiang Prefecture, where Haode's elder brother Houde serves as prefect. His feelings lay in partial indulgence, and his investigation was not factual."

Attendant Censor for Documents Quan Wanji impeached Zhang Yungu: "Yungu's household is registered in Xiang Prefecture, where Haode's elder brother Houde is prefect. His feelings lay in partial indulgence, and his investigation was not factual."
治書侍御史 is Attendant Censor for Documents (as repaired at s0185); 貫 refers to household registration.

In winter, in the tenth month, on bingwu the emperor was hunting hares in the rear park. Left Palace Guard General Ashina Simi remonstrated, "Heaven has made Your Majesty the father and mother of Chinese and barbarian alike—why treat your life so lightly!"

In winter, in the tenth month, on bingwu the emperor was hunting hares in the rear park. General of the Left Lingjun Guard Zhishi Sili remonstrated, "Heaven has made Your Majesty the father and mother of Chinese and barbarian alike—why treat your life so lightly!"
執失思力 is Zhishi Sili, not "Ashina Simi" (cf. the literal layer).
When the emperor was about to hunt deer again, Simi stripped off his headcloth, loosened his belt, knelt in blocking remonstrance, and the emperor desisted.
When the emperor was about to hunt deer again, Sili stripped off his headcloth, loosened his belt, knelt in firm remonstrance, and the emperor desisted.
思力 is Sili (Zhishi Sili), not "Simi".
